title: harness-catalog-and-eval-choreography-for-versioned-model-profiles
creator: Aisha Ramanujan
description: Goal: evolve the benchmark harness to produce deterministic, versioned performance profiles that can be published to the model catalog and used for automated gating during onboarding. This ticket covers a) a concise manifest schema for dataset/prompt/eval-runner composition, b) a lightweight cataloging layer for canonical datasets and prompt variants, and c) a choreographed eval runner interface (single-run contract + reproducibility metadata) so profiles are comparable across model builds and pinned versions. The resulting artifacts should include both performance metrics (latency quantiles, throughput, cost proxies) and fidelity traces (sampled outputs + eval scores) with stable identifiers suitable for pinning to model versions.
acceptance_criteria: A schema (YAML/JSON) that expresses: dataset id, dataset split, prompt variant id, eval runner id, seed, concurrency/sequence params and expected resource footprint
Harness can run the same manifest twice and produce byte-identical hashable profile metadata when seeds and runtime config are identical
Profiles contain standardized metric buckets: p50/p90/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec, avg and 95th memory (MB), tokens-per-dollar estimate, and eval scores per prompt-set
Profiles publish to S3 path and register in model-catalog with model version tag, including an immutable artifact URL and human-friendly summary
CI job can fetch published profile for a PR and fail gating if regression > configured thresholds
Docs and quickstart for platform teams to add a new canonical dataset and a new eval runner implementation
implementation_steps: Design minimal manifest schema and validate with examples (small LLM toy model + sample dataset)
Implement catalog service stub: CRUD for canonical dataset and prompt variants, with unique IDs and metadata (license, provenance)
Add eval-runner interface in harness: init(config), run_batch(inputs), collect_metrics(), write_profile(output_path)
Wire deterministic RNG and request ordering logic; persist run-seed in profile metadata
Extend profile schema to include 'pinning_id' that maps to model registry version tags
Add publisher: upload artifacts to S3, create model-catalog record and emit webhook event for CI
Create CI gating job that compares baseline profile to candidate and applies deciders (latency/cost/score thresholds)
Author docs + examples and run a handoff demo with DX and Platform teams
notes: We want to avoid coupling the manifest to a particular runner implementation. Keep the contract minimal: inputs (dataset rows + prompt template), RNG seed, runner config. Runner takes responsibility for batching and hardware hints. Profiles must include provenance: git commit, build image, docker digest, and CUDA/cuDNN tags where relevant.
risks: Large datasets will inflate CI runtimes — include small 'smoke' manifests and a policy to only gate on smoke for PRs while nightly full-profile runs produce production artifacts. Edge cases: nondeterministic eval-runners (external API calls) must be wrapped with recorded responses (VCR-style) or flagged in catalog.
testing_plan: Unit tests for manifest validation, integration test that runs harness against a toy model and checks profile hash stability, e2e that publishes to a staging catalog and triggers CI compare job. Add a golden manifest checked into repo for regression detection.
observability: Profiles should link to per-route latency histograms in Console; publish a summary dashboard (p50/p90/p99) per model-version and a CI alert if regressions detected. Store raw metrics as NDJSON alongside summarized JSON for future analysis.
